- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is high, apply downward correction of 5–15% to reflect risk.  
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling), reduce forecast peak by 10–20% for next period.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high) should be capped at +5% to avoid overestimating volatility.  
- Forecast should align with sentiment trend: if sentiment is rising, allow slight upward bias; if falling, allow downward bias — but never exceed 10% deviation from sentiment-weighted average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 10% of forecast range, consider underestimating next period’s volatility.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.35+ swings), reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average) to avoid noise-driven spikes.
